description: Kart bwrap mount policy — TEMPLATE. Copy to $WILLOW_HOME/kart-sandbox.json and add this box's own repositories to bind_try. Extend bind_try / env_prefixes for new paths without code changes.

_template.what_this_is: The mount policy a sandboxed Kart task runs under: what it may open, what it may write, and what it must never see. This file is the shape; an instance is a box's own copy with its repositories filled in. Nothing here names a person, a home directory, or a machine.
_template.resolution_order: $KART_SANDBOX_CONFIG → $WILLOW_HOME/kart-sandbox.json → the vendored default in kartikeya. A box that has never been configured runs the vendored one.

tokens.{{WILLOW_SAFE_ROOT}}: the SAFE app store root, when present

_template.packaging: Everything below is portable. An instance adds repository paths and nothing else, which is what lets this ship inside an APK, a wheel, or a container image without carrying somebody's filesystem with it.

rtk_compress._note: Off by default. rtk-plus rewrites a shell command to its own compressing wrapper before Kart executes it. Enable only after observing it on real tasks.

_policy.bind_try_is_read_write: bind_try entries are READ-WRITE. This is the single most misread line in the file: a path added 'so a task can see it' is a path a task can also change. If a task only needs to read, the entry belongs in bind_try_read_only. Every failure below is a variation on that sentence.
_policy.one_repo_per_entry_never_a_parent: List repositories INDIVIDUALLY. Never bind a parent directory to catch several at once. A parent bind grants whatever is added to that directory later, including things nobody meant to expose — and on a box where a personal data store shares a parent with source repositories, one convenient entry silently republishes it. It also reorders the mount sequence, which can defeat a read-only overlay applied to a subpath.
_policy.the_sovereign_store_is_absent_on_purpose: A user's own data vault does not appear in this file, and its absence is a DECISION rather than an omission. Record that where a later reader will find it, because silence is indistinguishable from oversight — and a sandboxed task pointed at a store that is not mounted opens a root that is not there and reads an EMPTY store while passing every gate on the way.
_policy.secret_files_need_their_own_overlay: The trust-root overlay applied by the sandbox covers the manifest ACLs and the consent files — and nothing else. Every other sensitive file inside the fleet home sits in a read-write mount. Measured on a live box 2026-09-01: the manifest directory was correctly read-only while the RECEIPT LEDGER and the SECRET STORE were writable, so a task could rewrite the very receipts recording what it did. List those files in bind_try_read_only, which acts as an overlay over the read-write mount. Verified after: a real append to the receipt database raises, while the store, logs and heartbeat stay writable.
_policy.work_root_is_not_the_product: CLOSED 2026-09-02. WILLOW_ROOT resolves to the product's source on a developer box and to site-packages on a pip install, and binding it read-write let a task edit the code that decides what tasks may do. Measured from inside a task on a live box: gate.py (the manifest ACL), pyproject.toml (the dependency floor that ships the sandbox's own overlays), .git and .gitignore were all WRITABLE while mcp_apps/ and consent.json were correctly read-only — the policy files protected and the code reading them not. WILLOW_ROOT is now read-only and {{WILLOW_ROOT}}/worktrees is the writable lane: a task that needs to change source works in a worktree. Requires kartikeya with ensure_work_root(), which creates the lane — a bind target that does not exist is dropped, not created.
_policy.credentials_are_gated_not_bound: Credential environment prefixes, the gh config and netrc reach a task only on allow_net. A no-network task gets zero credentials. Keep it that way.
_policy.private_keys_never_enter: SSH private keys are never bound; git over SSH uses the agent socket. The same rule covers any other authentication key the host holds — an adb key, a signing key, a device credential. A build toolchain may be bound; the key that signs its output may not.
_policy.tmpfs_not_host: /tmp and /dev/shm are private tmpfs, never host binds.
_policy.localhost_tier: allow_localhost shares the host network namespace so a loopback model server works, while still stripping credentials. Weaker than full isolation; prefer it over allow_net for embedding-only work.
_policy.never_list_the_work_root_read_write: WILLOW_ROOT must not ALSO appear in bind_try or bind_read_write. A path collision resolves as (existing_ro and new_ro), so a read-write entry wins over a read-only one no matter which is listed first — one convenient per-repo entry for the product repo silently undoes the read-only work root while this file still reads correct. Two such entries were live on a real box. Newer kartikeya logs the promotion; do not rely on reading the config to notice it.
_policy.venvs_are_read_only: A writable venv lets a task rewrite the .pth that resolves the product package — work_root_is_not_the_product through a different door. Venvs are bound read-only and .venv-dev is deliberately not in bind_try.

_instance_notes.add_your_repositories: Append this box's checkouts to bind_try, one entry per repository, following one_repo_per_entry_never_a_parent. Nothing else in this file needs to change to stand a box up.
_instance_notes.add_your_secret_files: Append the fleet home's sensitive files to bind_try_read_only per secret_files_need_their_own_overlay. Until template_keys_required lands these must be written as literal paths, because a token that does not resolve binds NOTHING AND SAYS NOTHING.
_instance_notes.template_keys_required: {{WILLOW_HOME}} and a work-root token are not yet known to the template context, which today resolves only HOME, WILLOW_ROOT, WILLOW_GROVE_ROOT, WILLOW_SAFE_ROOT, WILLOW_AGENTS_ROOT and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Three of those historically pointed at paths that no longer existed. An unresolved token fails silently — the same shape as every other failure in this file.
